title: WORKSHEET 12
subject: Simple Past vs Present Perfect Tense
subjectVi: Ngữ pháp bài 12: Simple Past vs Present Perfect Tense

sections.instruction: Use the SIMPLE PAST or the PRESENT PERFECT TENSE to fill in the blanks:

questions.prompt: What [gap] (you / learn) since you [gap] (come) here? How many friends [gap] (you / make)? I hope you [gap] (already / meet) a lot of interesting people.
acceptedAnswers: have you learned|have you learnt / came / have you made / have already met
questions.explanation: since + past point → present perfect; since you came (past)

questions.prompt: Last night my roommate and I [gap] (have) some free time, so we [gap] (go) to a show.
questions.explanation: last night → simple past

questions.prompt: I [gap] (just / have) lunch, but I [gap] (not / have) lunch yesterday.
questions.explanation: just → present perfect; yesterday → simple past

questions.prompt: Who [gap] (write) the play “Hamlet”?
questions.explanation: finished past event → simple past

questions.prompt: How many games [gap] (the team / win) so far this season?
questions.explanation: so far → present perfect

questions.prompt: I don’t know Carol’s husband. I [gap] (never / meet) him.
questions.explanation: never (up to now) → present perfect

questions.prompt: It [gap] (rain) a lot last week, but it [gap] (not / rain) much so far this week.
questions.explanation: last week → past; so far → present perfect

questions.prompt: How many letters [gap] (you / write) since the beginning of the month?
questions.explanation: since → present perfect

questions.prompt: When we were on vacation, the weather [gap] (be) terrible.
questions.explanation: finished past time → simple past

questions.prompt: In her whole lifetime, Mary [gap] (never / see) snow.
questions.explanation: life experience up to now → present perfect

questions.prompt: I don’t know where Ammy is. [gap] (you / see) her?
questions.explanation: recent, no time given → present perfect

questions.prompt: When I [gap] (get) home last night, I [gap] (be) very tired and I [gap] (go) straight to bed.
questions.explanation: last night → simple past

questions.prompt: Your car looks very clean. [gap] (you / wash) it?
questions.explanation: result now → present perfect

questions.prompt: George [gap] (not / be) very well last week.
questions.explanation: last week → simple past

questions.prompt: Mr. Clark [gap] (work) in a bank for 15 years. Then he gave it up.
questions.explanation: finished period in the past → simple past

sections.instruction: Use the PRESENT PERFECT TENSE or the PRESENT PERFECT CONTINUOUS to fill in the blanks:

questions.prompt: I’m trying to study. I [gap] (try) to study for the last hour, but something always seems to interrupt me. I think I’d better go to the library.
questions.explanation: ongoing activity for a period → continuous

questions.prompt: The children are playing basketball right now. They [gap] (play) for almost two hours. They must be getting tired.
questions.explanation: ongoing activity for a period → continuous

questions.prompt: The telephone [gap] (ring) four times in the last hour, and each time it has been for my roommate.
questions.explanation: number of times → present perfect simple

questions.prompt: The telephone [gap] (ring) for almost a minute. Why doesn’t someone answer it?
questions.explanation: ongoing activity for a period → continuous

questions.prompt: It [gap] (rain) all day. I wonder when it will stop.
questions.explanation: ongoing activity all day → continuous

questions.prompt: We [gap] (have) three accidents so far this week. I wonder how many more we will have if you keep using the tools carelessly.
questions.explanation: how many so far → present perfect simple

questions.prompt: We [gap] (live) here since last June.
questions.explanation: live + since: both forms possible

questions.prompt: My little son is dirty from head to foot because he [gap] (play) in the mud.
questions.explanation: activity with a visible result → continuous

questions.prompt: What’s the matter? Your eyes are red and puffy. I hope you [gap] (not / cry). Oh, now I understand. You [gap] (peel) some onions.
acceptedAnswers: haven't been crying / have been peeling
questions.explanation: recent activity with visible result → continuous

questions.prompt: Hello, Rob. I’m happy to see you again. I [gap] (not / see) you for weeks. What [gap] you [gap] (do) lately?
questions.explanation: see → simple; lately activity → continuous

questions.prompt: I [gap] (not / be) able to reach my boss on the phone yet. I [gap] (try) for the last twenty minutes, but the line [gap] (be) busy.
acceptedAnswers: haven't been / have been trying / has been
questions.explanation: state verb be → simple; try for a period → continuous

questions.prompt: We [gap] (have) three major snowstorms so far this winter. I wonder how many more we will have.
questions.explanation: how many so far → present perfect simple

questions.prompt: I [gap] (write) them three times, but I still haven’t received a reply.
questions.explanation: number of times → present perfect simple

questions.prompt: A: Dr. Harrison is a good teacher. How long [gap] he [gap] (be) at the university? B: He [gap] (teach) here for almost 25 years.
acceptedAnswers: has / been / has been teaching|has taught
questions.explanation: be (state) → simple; teach for a period → continuous

questions.prompt: A: What are you going to order for dinner? B: Well, I [gap] (have / have) pizza. So I think, I’ll order that.
questions.explanation: have (eat) in present perfect: have had

questions.prompt: My uncle [gap] (paint) the outside of his house for three weeks and he’s still not finished.
questions.explanation: unfinished activity → continuous

questions.prompt: The Smiths are presently in Tunisia. They [gap] (travel) throughout North Africa since the middle of May. They’ll return home in another month.
questions.explanation: ongoing activity since a point → continuous

sections.instruction: Use the PRESENT PERFECT TENSE or the PRESENT PERFECT CONTINUOUS to fill in the blanks:

questions.prompt: I’m tired. We [gap] (walk) for over an hour. Let’s stop and rest for a while.
questions.explanation: activity for a period, effect now → continuous

questions.prompt: The zoo isn’t far from here. I [gap] (walk) there many times.
questions.explanation: many times → present perfect simple

questions.prompt: I [gap] (write) my friends at least a dozen letters since I left home and came here.
questions.explanation: how many → present perfect simple

questions.prompt: Sally is writing a letter to her boyfriend. She [gap] (write) it since she got home from class. It’s going to be a long letter.
questions.explanation: unfinished activity since a point → continuous

questions.prompt: The telephone [gap] (ring) four times in the last hour, and each time it has been for my roommate.
questions.explanation: number of times → present perfect simple

questions.prompt: The telephone [gap] (ring) for almost a minute. Why doesn’t someone answer it?
questions.explanation: ongoing activity for a period → continuous

questions.prompt: She is 80 and she [gap] (never / read) a book in her life.
questions.explanation: life experience → present perfect simple

questions.prompt: The secretary is very tired. She [gap] (type) all morning.
questions.explanation: activity all morning, effect now → continuous

questions.prompt: Tom is reading a book. He started two hours ago and he is on page 53. He [gap] (read) for two hours.
questions.explanation: how long → continuous

questions.prompt: Hello! I [gap] (clean) the windows. So far I [gap] (clean) five of them and there are two more to do.
questions.explanation: activity → continuous; how many so far → simple

questions.prompt: My grandfather [gap] (die) 30 years ago. I [gap] (never / meet) him.
questions.explanation: ago → simple past; his life is finished

questions.prompt: A: Is your father at home? B: No, I’m afraid he [gap] (go) out. A: When exactly [gap] (he / go) out? B: About ten minutes ago.
questions.explanation: result now → present perfect; when → simple past

sections.instruction: Use the SIMPLE PAST or the PRESENT PERFECT TENSE to fill in the blanks:

questions.prompt: The young man [gap] (never / be) to Paris, but he [gap] (read) a book about this city last year.
questions.explanation: never → present perfect; last year → simple past

questions.prompt: [gap] you [gap] (decide) where to go yet?
questions.explanation: yet → present perfect

questions.prompt: A: Have some tea, please. B: No, thank you. I [gap] (just / have) two cups of tea.
questions.explanation: just → present perfect

questions.prompt: Susan [gap] (do) her homework before 10 o’clock but Jane [gap] (not / write) a word until now.
questions.explanation: until now → present perfect

questions.prompt: Her mother [gap] (buy) her a pair of new shoes yesterday.
questions.explanation: yesterday → simple past

questions.prompt: The Prime Minister [gap] (leave) for the USA an hour ago.
questions.explanation: ago → simple past

questions.prompt: A: [gap] the plane [gap] (land)? B: Yes, it [gap] (land) ten minutes ago.
questions.explanation: no time → present perfect; ago → simple past

questions.prompt: It [gap] (not / rain) for a long time.
questions.explanation: for + period up to now → present perfect

questions.prompt: [gap] you [gap] (see) my dog? It [gap] (run away) this morning.
acceptedAnswers: Have / seen / ran away|has run away
questions.explanation: no time → present perfect; this morning → past

questions.prompt: We [gap] (meet) at a party a long time ago, but I [gap] (not / see) her since then.
questions.explanation: ago → simple past; since then → present perfect

questions.prompt: I [gap] (see) an interesting book in a bookshop yesterday, but I [gap] (not / buy) it.
questions.explanation: yesterday → simple past

questions.prompt: My friend [gap] (fall) from the bicycle because he [gap] (not / ride) one for ages.
questions.explanation: earlier past → past perfect (or present perfect if now)

questions.prompt: His father [gap] (die) in 1970, but he [gap] (never / visit) his father’s grave since that time.
questions.explanation: in 1970 → past; since that time → present perfect

questions.prompt: They [gap] (go) to America years ago, but none of them [gap] (come) back since then.
questions.explanation: ago → past; since then → present perfect

questions.prompt: A: [gap] you [gap] (speak) to an Englishman? B: Yes, I [gap] (have) a short conversation with one last night.
questions.explanation: experience → present perfect; last night → past

questions.prompt: A: [gap] you ever [gap] (be) to Tatilya? B: Yes, I [gap] (go) there two years ago.
questions.explanation: ever → present perfect; ago → simple past

questions.prompt: A: [gap] you [gap] (see) Jane recently? B: No, I [gap] (see) her for a long time.
questions.explanation: recently / for a long time → present perfect

sections.instruction: Rewrite the sentences using the SIMPLE PAST or the PRESENT PERFECT TENSE: (Example: I haven’t seen her for a long time. → It’s ages since I saw her.)

questions.prompt: I last met George two weeks ago. → I haven’t
acceptedAnswers: I haven't met George for two weeks.
I haven't seen George for two weeks.
I haven't met him for two weeks.
questions.explanation: last … ago → haven't + participle + for

questions.prompt: They have been here for three months. → They arrived
acceptedAnswers: They arrived here three months ago.
questions.explanation: for (up to now) → simple past + ago

questions.prompt: We started living in Istanbul 12 years ago. → We have
acceptedAnswers: We have lived in Istanbul for 12 years.
We've lived in Istanbul for 12 years.
We have been living in Istanbul for 12 years.
We've been living in Istanbul for 12 years.
We have lived in Istanbul for twelve years.
We've lived in Istanbul for twelve years.
We have been living in Istanbul for twelve years.
We've been living in Istanbul for twelve years.
questions.explanation: started … ago → have lived + for

questions.prompt: I last saw my girlfriend five days ago. → I haven’t
acceptedAnswers: I haven't seen my girlfriend for five days.
I haven't seen her for five days.
questions.explanation: last … ago → haven't + participle + for

questions.prompt: Is this the first time you have tasted a kiwi? → Use (not) + you, and end with “one before?”
acceptedAnswers: Have you not tasted one before?
Haven't you ever tasted one before?
questions.explanation: first time → haven't … before

questions.prompt: I last smoked a cigarette ten years ago. → I haven’t
acceptedAnswers: I haven't smoked a cigarette for ten years.
I haven't smoked for ten years.
questions.explanation: last … ago → haven't + participle + for

questions.prompt: I last drank wine two weeks ago. → Start with “It’s two weeks” and end with “wine”.
acceptedAnswers: It's two weeks since I last drank wine.
It's two weeks since I drank wine.
It's been two weeks since I last drank wine.
questions.explanation: It's + period + since + simple past

questions.prompt: I have lived in Istanbul since January. → I (come)
acceptedAnswers: I came to Istanbul in January.
questions.explanation: since + point → simple past + in

questions.prompt: They moved to Ankara two years ago. → Start with “They” and end with “two years”.
acceptedAnswers: They have lived in Ankara for two years.
They've lived in Ankara for two years.
They have been living in Ankara for two years.
They've been living in Ankara for two years.
They have been in Ankara for two years.
They've been in Ankara for two years.
questions.explanation: moved … ago → have lived + for

questions.prompt: She hasn’t been to Rome before. → This is the first time
acceptedAnswers: This is the first time she has been to Rome.
This is the first time she's been to Rome.
This is the first time she has ever been to Rome.
This is the first time she's ever been to Rome.
questions.explanation: the first time + present perfect
